items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I was to share a melody with him. So we got a chance to play in a rehearsal... I mean hey, I’ve played with Clark Terry so why not?

ctx.x: Right. And then you ran into Clark Terry here.

Oh my, you are fast forwarding to the next epiphany. Oh man, yeah. Clark Terry. This was in April of 1994. And you know it’s funny, last night at the concert featuring Dick Hyman, Randy Sandke — a group led by Hyman and featuring yourself — I got a chance to see for the first time in 30 years Don Cantwell, who I studied saxophone with here, and who was the head of the Hamilton jazz band. And so he made arrangements for Clark to come. Now he reminded me last night that the fraternity — is it Delta Upsilon? — DU —…

mean it was literally like being in heaven. And I mean I’m telling you from that point my playing improved automatically in this sense: I began to project more of my own personality, you know, I wasn’t holding back as much. Be yourself. Say what you’ve got to say. I mean hey, I’ve played with Clark Terry so why not?
